etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: From Middle English, borrowed from Latin serēnus (“clear, cloudless, untroubled”).
senses: Without worry or anxiety; unaffected by disturbance.

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
paragraphs: Borrowed from Middle French serein, from Old French serein (“evening”), from Vulgar Latin *serānum, from substantive use of sērum, neuter of sērus (“late”) + -ānus suffix.
senses: A fine rain from a cloudless sky after sunset.
